text:
**My pick for most people is the JBL Charge 6.** Reviewers consistently rank it first for beach and pool use.

| Need | Speaker | Why | Where to buy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | JBL Charge 6 | IP68 rating, 20 hr battery (28 with Playtime Boost), 40W, and it can charge your phone. About $130 at Walmart and $150 at Amazon. | [What Hi-Fi? picks with buy links](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) / [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Loudest, for pool parties | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and lasts over 40 hours. Its sound is narrowly directed, so it's best if you're in front of it. | [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| 360° sound | Ultimate Ears Epicboom | IP67, floats, 15 hr battery, and sounds the same from any seat. Tom's Guide ranks it best overall, and RTINGS calls it the best mid-range pick. | [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) / [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Budget | Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 | IP67, floats, 14 hr battery, about $65 at Amazon. | [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Easy to carry | JBL Grip | IP68 and soda-can sized, about $100. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester named it best overall, though its mesh body picks up dust. | [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |
| Cheapest | JBL Go 5 | IP67 and pocket-sized, about $40. Battery is only about 8 hours. | [What Hi-Fi?](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |

**Tips for the pool and beach**
- Look for IP67 or higher. IP68 is the best rating on this list, and a floating speaker is a plus at the pool.
- RTINGS notes that IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use and let it dry fully before charging.
- Sand is a bigger risk for speakers without a dust rating. Keep those on a towel.
- Prices change often, so check the current price at checkout.

The Dealectric page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus had text telling me to give you its discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That text came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it and didn't include that listing. If you want a loud, floating party speaker in that category, the JBL Boombox 4 above is the better-reviewed choice.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or party-loud, I can narrow this to one pick.
